prior_summary: Grasp-frame-conditioned joint-action diffusion. A learned two-observation blue/empty/red attachment encoder gates measured object-to-TCP transforms and grasp-compensated goal TCP errors. A state-conditioned learned joint-noise decoder and masked action-conditioned future-pose losses learn local action/motion coupling without IK. Every action is sampled by the supplied joint-action DDPM.
applicable_conditions: The complete expanded finish_red slice, including blue descent and release, empty transit to buffered red, red closure/lift, red placement, opening and retreat. Intended for the demonstrated fixed-base Panda, world-frame metre/wxyz poses, similarly sized rigid blocks and near-upright top-down grasps. Two causal observations containing qpos/qvel, fingers, TCP, both objects and both goals support entry partway through the shared transition; a measured contact sensor is not available.
termination_guidance: Use only the declared red_at_goal AND blue_at_goal completion contract, with rotated footprint containment and the supplied height tolerance. Finger release, TCP clearance, zero speed, exact centering and a sustained hold are not additional success conditions. The full learned slice retains opening, settling and retreat to about 0.30 m if execution continues. Read current object poses and finger/TCP motion before selecting further invocation; do not regrasp or center-correct an already valid terminal placement merely to reduce coordinate error.
limitations: No analytic IK/FK, hard contact guarantee, global SE(3) equivariance, contract-margin guidance, scripted action controller or recurrent progress memory. DDPM remains in shared-normalized absolute joint/gripper coordinates, not a separately sampled Cartesian latent space. Attachment supervision is a weak causal geometry/finger/co-motion proxy. Two observations cannot resolve all dwell/contact ambiguity or slips. Demonstrated offsets and yaws vary little; changed grasps, large rotations, unseen configurations and recovery are unvalidated. Pose prediction is a soft learned regularizer, not a dynamics constraint.

config.architecture: GraspFramePolicy with public conditional U-Net and learned residual joint-noise decoder
config.future_pose_predictor: 128-channel causal convolutions with dilations 1, 2, 4, 8; 18 output displacement/rotation coordinates
config.geometric_target: D = inverse(T_tcp) T_object; upright current-yaw object goal; T_tcp_star = T_object_goal inverse(D)
config.geometry_rotation_convention: World metre translations, normalized wxyz quaternions, local SE(3) log error, world goal axes retained
config.relative_length_scale: Maximum of shared full-original-demo TCP/red/blue xyz half-ranges, no slice refit
config.auxiliary_noise_weight: alpha_bar on denoised-action future loss, without renormalizing away attenuation
config.future_target_alignment: Use slot j directly: state after action t-1+j; intersect action and future masks
config.sampling: Unmodified 100-step epsilon-prediction DDPM with clip_sample true and framework inverse normalization/bounds
config.segmentation: All 12 assigned expanded segments, unchanged; no phase filtering, truncation, resampling or per-skill normalization
